overall: No violation found. The request for minutes fell under the Open Meeting Law and was answered within 10 days, since only shorthand notes existed; the chair controls whether public comment is allowed.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to timely respond to a March 21, 2025 emailed request for minutes of its March 19, 2025 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that draft minutes of the March 19, 2025, minutes did not yet exist at the time of the request and therefore the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when Mr. Doane responded within two hours of receiving the request without providing copies of minutes.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly does not allow the public to submit questions or comment during meetings.
allegations.key_passage: The Law does not require that a public body allow public participation; rather, the Law gives the chair of the public body discretion to decide whether to permit public comment during a meeting, and if public comment will be permitted, to set restrictions on public comment.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
